questions.question: First-sentence voice: must an exported symbol's TSDoc first sentence be third-person (`Creates`, `Escapes`), making imperative openings (`Create`, `Escape`) drift?
questions.rule_quote: The first sentence states what the symbol does in the third person with an `-s` verb — `Creates`, `Returns`, `Checks whether` — and never repeats the symbol's name.
questions.fleet_reading: The rule is literal and unambiguous, and the fleet contradicts it almost everywhere. Doc blocks immediately preceding an `export function` / exported arrow across 48 fleet packages plus scaffold: third-person=442, imperative=1507. 33 packages are exclusively imperative, 6 exclusively third-person, 10 mixed. Per-package third/imperative: scaffold 7/116, contract 1/215, browser 1/139, reason 0/139, database 0/66, workflow 0/51, middleware 4/48, markdown 20/43, interpret 0/42, toolbox 0/42, server 0/38, terminal 0/38, console 0/37, msg 1/36, program 0/36, html 11/35, brief 1/33, csv 2/33, qualifier 0/33, sea 2/33, form 0/32, agent 0/30, table 0/25, router 0/23, rater 0/22 — against mcp 168/0, test 101/0, process 38/0, probe 32/0, lsp 28/0, codec 25/0. Fleet-wide leading words confirm the split: Determine 246, Create 168, Build 152, Narrow 99, Compile 70, Decode 60, Read 58, Resolve 54, against Determines 87, Creates 52, Checks 52, Reads 44. No commit in the available (shallow) history migrates a package between voices; each package was authored in one voice and left there, so no deliberate fleet convention displaces the rule. No gate enforces the rule: `configs/policy.ts` and `tests/policy.test.ts` contain no check on TSDoc voice. Scope note for per-package rulings: the canon repository is itself 116 imperative to 7 third-person, so a DRIFT finding raised against one package is selective enforcement of a fleet-wide condition.

questions.question: Boolean `@returns` form: must a boolean-returning guard's `@returns` be written "True if …; false otherwise"?
questions.rule_quote: Describe a boolean parameter as "If `true`, …; if `false`, …", and a boolean return as "True if …; false otherwise".
questions.fleet_reading: The rule prescribes a literal phrasing, and the neighbouring rule line does the same shape ("Write a default as \"Default: …\" and a thrown error as \"Thrown when …\""), so read it as exact wording rather than as content guidance. The fleet overwhelmingly uses a different form. Boolean `@returns` openings across 48 fleet packages plus scaffold: "True if"=47, "`true` when/for/only when"=325, "Whether"=117; "false otherwise" appears 57 times fleet-wide. Only codec (7), lsp (19), probe (14), and test (7) use the prescribed form, and each of those is one of the six all-third-person packages. Per-package "True if"/backtick-`true`/"Whether": scaffold 0/25/2, reason 0/44/0, mcp 0/40/37, table 0/22/11, contract 0/16/0, middleware 0/16/0, program 0/15/0, html 0/14/0, interpret 0/13/0, markdown 0/13/0, rater 0/11/0, server 0/10/0, agent 0/9/0, csv 0/7/0, qualifier 0/7/0, database 0/5/18, form 0/1/16, workspace 0/0/6, browser 0/0/6, pool 0/0/3. The canon repository is the largest single violator at 0 conforming against 25 backtick-`true`. No gate enforces the form. The dominant fleet form does state the true branch ("`true` when the value is X") but does not spell the false branch, so it is a genuine departure from the prescribed wording rather than a synonym of it.

questions.question: `@example` import specifiers: must a public TSDoc `@example` block import from `@orkestrel/<name>`, making `@src/*` aliases in source examples drift under documentation.md?
questions.rule_quote:
Code fences import through the package's published specifier:

- primary/core API: `@orkestrel/<name>`;
- secondary environment API: `@orkestrel/<name>/<environment>`.

Never use in-repository `@src/*` aliases in public guide examples; reserve them for source/tests.
questions.fleet_reading: The findings misread the cited rule. It sits under the heading `## Guide examples`, its ban names "public guide examples", and its own second clause reserves `@src/*` "for source/tests" — so on its literal text it does not reach a TSDoc `@example` block inside a source file, and it arguably permits `@src/*` there. History confirms that reading was applied deliberately: reason commit 3e6bca5 "docs: guide fences import the published specifier" (2026-07-20) rewrote `guides/src/reason.md` only and left every `src` TSDoc example on `@src/core`; console carries the same commit 175a3b7. The enforcement boundary matches: `tests/guides.test.ts:189` checks specifiers in guide fences and no gate reads TSDoc `@example` at all. The findings' factual half is nonetheless confirmed. Doc-comment specifiers across 48 fleet packages plus scaffold: `@src/*`=331 in 19 packages, `@orkestrel/*`=533 in 34 packages. Those blocks ship: fleet/reason/dist/src/core/index.d.ts carries 150 `@example` tags and 148 `from '@src/core'`; interpret 55, toolbox 22, agent 21, console 16, markdown 14, router 10, template 8. `package.json` `files` is `["dist/src","README.md"]` and `exports["."].import.types` resolves into `dist/src`, so a consumer's editor reads a specifier only this repository's `tsconfig.json` paths resolve. Canon scaffold/src is 139 `@orkestrel/*` to 0 `@src/*`, so `@orkestrel/<name>` is the canon form — but as authored practice, not as anything this rule says. Route the shipping defect to a new rule that names published `@example` blocks; do not raise it as drift against documentation.md § Guide examples.
